entries.snippet: Clayton-Thomas was a onetime street fighter and petty thief from Canada who briefly became a rock superstar.

entries.title: Weinstein's New York rape charge dropped after accuser says she can't endure a 4th trial
entries.snippet: The movie mogul still stands convicted of another sexual felony in New York and others in California, and he remains behind bars. But the New York rape charge had remained unresolved after an overturned conviction followed by two hung juries.

entries.title: South African civil groups warn of dire impact as U.S. phases out HIV program funding

entries.title: India news: Government sends help to quake-hit Venezuela

entries.snippet: The Bayreuth Festival had canceled a planned memorial lecture featuring Jewish author and broadcaster Michel Friedman, drawing sharp criticism.

entries.title: Bayer: Why so many Roundup weedkiller lawsuits?

entries.title: Balochistan activist's life sentence raises fear of unrest
entries.snippet: With the conviction of a leading rights campaigner, Pakistan has drawn criticism from rights groups and sparked fears it could deepen unrest in Balochistan and weaken trust in peaceful activism.

entries.snippet: Two storms were set to converge above Japan, prompting officials to issue landslide warnings and evacuation orders for hundreds of thousands of people.

entries.title: Japan needs more foreign workers, but many feel unwelcome
entries.snippet: While Japan faces a deepening labor shortage and growing demand for foreign workers, it has been moving to tighten visa rules and regulations.

entries.title: Montenegro arrests Iran-linked hacker wanted by US
entries.snippet: The FBI was helping the Montenegrin police detain an Iranian-Turkish national whose cyberattacks on US infrastructure allegedly caused billions in damages.

entries.title: Fact check: As Europe bakes, should you trust your sunscreen?
entries.snippet: As a heatwave sweeps across Europe, claims are resurfacing online questioning whether sunscreen is safe or linked to skin cancer risk.

entries.title: Sudan: Fears of atrocities as RSF surrounds key city
entries.snippet: As Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces mass around the strategic city of el-Obeid, fears are growing of atrocities similar to those seen in Darfur's el-Fasher. Could sanctions still prevent bloodshed?

entries.title: Singapore: French teen in trouble over straw-licking video
entries.snippet: A French student is accused of licking a straw at a juice vending machine before putting it back and posting the video online. He faces jail time if convicted in Singapore, a country famous for its tough laws.

entries.title: Germany news: Berlin's orchestra eases dress code amid heat
entries.snippet: Men are not obliged to wear jackets during the orchestra's end-of-season performance this weekend. Meanwhile, a court has sentenced the defendent in the Magdeburg Christmas market attack to life. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Here's what southern Europeans know about surviving heat waves
entries.snippet: People in countries like Greece, Italy and Spain have long lived with high temperatures. Here's what more northerly countries can learn from them about managing heat waves as they become more common.

entries.title: Magdeburg Christmas market attacker sentenced to life in prison
entries.snippet: A Magdeburg court has sentenced a 51-year-old to life over his 2024 attack on a Christmas market in the city. The trained psychiatrist drove an SUV through a barricade and into a crowd, killing six and injuring hundreds.

entries.title: Europe heat wave 'virtually impossible' without human impact
entries.snippet: A new study says Europe's current heat wave would have been nearly impossible without human-driven climate change. And Germany is expecting things to warm up even more. DW has the latest.

entries.title: North Korea: Kim Jong Un oversees ballistic missile tests, calls for stronger 'offensive posture'
entries.snippet: Pyongyang tested "major weapons" as North Korea's leader called for greater strike capabilities along the border with South Korea.

entries.title: Death toll from twin earthquakes in Venezuela has more than doubled to 589, acting President Rodriguez says. Follow live
entries.snippet: Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said at least 589 people have died after two strong earthquakes rattled the capital and surrounding regions. DW has the latest.

entries.title: King Charles won't live in Buckingham Palace, reveals taxes
entries.snippet: Buckingham Palace has been the British monarch's official residence in London for nearly two centuries. But royal officials say King Charles and Queen Camilla won't reside there.

entries.title: Germany disappoints in loss to Ecuador at 2026 World Cup
entries.snippet: Germany had already qualified for the knockouts of the 2026 World Cup, but their performance was still disappointing in a 2-1 defeat.

entries.title: US Supreme Court sides with Bayer over Roundup cancer suits
entries.snippet: Bayer, which acquired Roundup in 2018, said the decision is good for science and farmers. The Supreme Court's ruling was met with backlash from both Republicans and Democrats.
